findings.summary: Round 2's inline finding was fixed on writeHeldBytes and left open on writeHeldBytesChunked -- the HELD+PROXY path, which is the one DefaultIngest takes for an 8 MiB segment it just wrote. No test anywhere throws from a sink while this pod holds the bytes, so that method's entire error handling is unconstrained.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, two mutations, each with :ingest:test AND :http:test AND :plugin:test green (0 failures in every result XML). (a) SubscriptionHub.java:486-500 -- delete writeHeldBytesChunked's try/catch and declare `throws IOException`: one throwing sink's IOException reaches deliver():435, becomes UncheckedIOException, NOBODY on the segment is completed, publish rethrows and pushLoop's `catch (RuntimeException e) { continue; }` drops the whole window for every healthy consumer. That is the exact mutation round 2 measured as (b) on the sibling method writeHeldBytes, which the new anINLINESinkThatTHROWS... test now kills; the same one on the chunked method survives. (b) SubscriptionHub.java:496 -- `live.remove(i)` to `return`: the first sink to throw abandons the rest of the segment for EVERYONE, and because the healthy sinks never threw their Tracking.failed is false, so deliver():440-450 COMPLETES them holding a PREFIX. That is verbatim the outcome deliver()'s own javadoc calls 'THE WORST OUTCOME AVAILABLE' and the outcome aSinkThatTHROWSMidSegmentIsNOTCompletedAndTheOthersStillAre exists to prevent -- but that test publishes with heldBytes==null, so it drives streamFromStore and never enters this method. The only test that does enter it with more than one sink is everySinkGetsTheFIRSTChunkBeforeAnyGetsTheSECOND:318, whose three sinks are lambdas that cannot throw. Round 2 named this region by line ('no test anywhere throws from a sink while this pod HOLDS the bytes, so writeHeldBytesChunked's live.remove(i) has no input that reaches it either') and it is still unreached. Backlog M5.45a itself says an 8 MiB segment 'is past both bounds and goes proxy -- which is the point', so this is the dominant production serving path, not an edge. The fix is one test: the existing FailingSink(1) plus two Collecting sinks published with heldSegmentKey/heldBytes non-null under the FetchPolicyConfig(1, 0, 1) serving already used at :335, asserting the healthy sinks get the whole segment AND are completed and the doomed one is not.

findings.summary: aSubscriberWhoseOPENThrowsDoesNotDenyTheOthers constrains only the CHECKED half of deliver's open() catch; narrowing that catch to IOException alone survives all three suites.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: SubscriptionHub.java:423 -- `catch (IOException | RuntimeException slowOrDeadSubscriber)` narrowed to `catch (IOException slowOrDeadSubscriber)` leaves :ingest:test, :http:test and :plugin:test green (0 failures). The test's only refusing subscriber at :288-290 throws `new IOException(...)`, so the RuntimeException arm has no input. The variable name and the class javadoc's headline invariant ('A SLOW OR DEAD SUBSCRIBER MUST NOT BLOCK A COMMIT') both claim the unchecked case, and in production an unchecked throw from open() is the likelier one -- a bounded executor's RejectedExecutionException, an NPE on a half-torn-down consumer -- with the same consequence the test's own javadoc names: the throw leaves publish, reaches pushLoop, and one consumer silently drops the commit for every other consumer of the segment. Adding a second refusing subscriber that throws an unchecked exception, in the same test, closes it.

findings.summary: aSegmentNOBODYSubscribesToCostsZEROReads kills the PAIR of early returns but not the opened.isEmpty() one on its own -- the case where subscribers exist and every one of them fails to open still buys a GET for nobody, unasserted.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: the round-2 mutation (both guards `&& false`) now DIES on this test -- good. But `if (opened.isEmpty() && false)` at SubscriptionHub.java:430 ALONE leaves :ingest:test, :http:test and :plugin:test green (0 failures), because the new test has no subscriber for the segment at all and so returns at targets.isEmpty():361 first. The surviving state is reachable and distinct: a batched delta names another pod's segment, this pod HAS subscribers for it, and every one of them throws from open() or returns null -- opened is then empty, streamFromStore runs, and SegmentProxy.streamTo's own javadoc says an empty list still READS. One GET bought for zero consumers, at a rate scaling with other pods' flushes. One added assertion -- the existing aSubscriberWhoseOPENThrows... test with EVERY subscriber refusing, asserting gets == 0 -- closes it. Minor rather than major because the common no-subscriber case is now covered and the cost is one GET rather than record loss.
